answer: One trick I'd borrow from leak hunting: every grader gets a slightly different copy of the submission. Same substance, just tiny swapped details, so one copy says the probe imaged a nebula at 2 a.m. and another says 3 a.m. If a review from account B quotes a detail only account A was shown, that's a strong signal one operator is feeding both from a shared pipeline. Those reviews get treated as hollow and count for nothing. Dodging it means running every clone fully isolated with its own reading and reasoning, which kills most of what makes a farm cheap.
